name: Fly.io
summary: Fly.io runs your app as full servers (Docker containers) in data centers close to your users, billed only for what you use.

free_plan_covers.note: Fly.io discontinued all free allowances on October 7, 2024; new accounts get only a one-time trial credit, not an ongoing free plan.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No fixed monthly plan exists; billing is pure pay-as-you-go per second, so there is no single 'cheapest plan' price to report. Smallest always-on VM runs roughly $2 to $4/month plus storage and bandwidth.

portability.note: Fly.io runs your own Docker image with no proprietary runtime, so the same container moves to any other Docker host.

runtime_model.note: Apps run as always-on Firecracker VMs (Machines) built from a Dockerfile, not request-triggered functions.

persistent_disk.note: Fly Volumes attach local persistent NVMe storage directly to a Machine, billed at $0.15/GB/month as part of normal usage.

long_lived_connections.note: Apps run as regular servers, so WebSocket connections are fully supported with no extra setup or third-party service.

background_workers.note: Any Machine can run a long-running process with no public port, separate from a web-facing app.

scheduled_jobs.note: Machines support a built-in --schedule flag for hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly runs; it is coarse interval scheduling, not full cron syntax.

framework_support.note: Fly.io publishes official guides and templates for Next.js and SvelteKit run as full Docker-based Node servers; static Vite apps deploy the same way.

setup.step: Install flyctl and run fly auth signup or fly auth login.
Run fly launch in your project directory; it detects your framework and generates a Dockerfile and fly.toml.
Set environment variables with fly secrets set KEY=value.
Run fly volumes create for any data that must persist, then fly deploy to build and ship the app.

builder_notes: There is no free plan; every app is billed per second from the first deploy, so budget a few dollars a month minimum before building.
You write and own the Dockerfile (fly launch can generate a starting one); nothing is auto-detected the way Vercel or Render does it.
Attach a Fly Volume for any data that must survive redeploys; without one, writes to a Machine's disk are lost on the next deploy.
